Top Generative AI Skills and Education Trends for 2025
======================================================

Early signs of value with gen AI
--------------------------------

From a technology perspective, [generative AI](https://aws.amazon.com/executive-insights/generative-ai-ml/) was the dominant topic of interest throughout 2024. Everywhere you turned, someone was talking about it and trying to understand the implications for their business. While we can expect more of the same in 2025, the conversation is evolving as many generative AI proof-of-concepts will move into production, or as more organizations [experiment with generative AI skills](https://aws.amazon.com/training/learn-about/generative-ai/) and explore AI trends in education for employees.

In fact, two out of three organizations said that they are increasing their investments in generative AI due to early signs of business value, according to a [Deloitte study](https://www2.deloitte.com/us/en/pages/consulting/articles/state-of-generative-ai-in-enterprise.html). The greater investment in generative AI means businesses will need more people with AI skills to execute on their AI strategies and roadmap, which in turn requires leaders to continue providing training for their employees in 2025. This underscores how AI skills are crucial for businesses seeking to stay competitive and the increasing importance of AI workforce development. We saw significant demand in 2024 from AWS’s customers and partners who want to help their employees gain AI fluency, which enabled us to train two million people globally with free generative AI skills in just one year – as part of Amazon’s AI Ready commitment. The demand for AI skills training will only continue to rise.

![Image 1: A glowing futuristic cube with intricate digital patterns, surrounded by a grid of neon blue lines.](https://d1.awsstatic.com/onedam/marketing-channels/website/aws/en_US/executive-insight/approved/images/dfc8c18a294181f42283b7cffd41e126.5e4fd7061e69f6ab2f1d90b3b975846baf2dcb49.jpeg)

Top 5 skills trends
-------------------

Let’s dive into five skills trends you can expect to impact you and your employee talent strategy this year.

### 1

![Image 2: A group of people collaborating in a modern office setting with laptops and notebooks on a wooden table.](https://d1.awsstatic.com/onedam/marketing-channels/website/aws/en_US/executive-insight/approved/images/3765ed72abf84f7c6b65255d82be8e2c.e8e9ec87f55aaf9fb511d13b46ba9b6890801207.jpeg)

### Generative AI skills remain critical, but don't neglect soft skills

As more companies adopt generative AI in their business to drive innovations and improve workflows, there’s no doubt that AI and leadership go hand in hand, with leaders spending more time understanding generative AI fundamentals. However, they will also refresh their soft skills like effective communication, decision-making, manager coaching, and change management. In fact, these AI soft skills complement the technical knowledge needed to harness AI effectively. With change comes uncertainty, and there’s a lot of pressure for leaders to help their workforce prepare for and understand the organization’s point of view on the generative AI evolution. Employees need clear guidance and encouragement to be part of the change—including the psychological safety to try new things and fail safely. Now’s the time to[harness the power of emotional intelligence](https://aws.amazon.com/executive-insights/content/emotional-intelligence/) and inspect your culture to ensure it supports ongoing learning, critical thinking, and experimentation at all levels of the organization. Generative AI is going to do more for us than we ever imagined. Build your organization’s culture anchored by these critical soft skills to accelerate your opportunities with generative AI.

### 2

![Image 3: Person wearing headphones and a hoodie, sitting at a desk with a glowing computer setup in a dimly lit room.](https://d1.awsstatic.com/onedam/marketing-channels/website/aws/en_US/executive-insight/approved/images/dd6dad9763cfdfe87603b91775e2c5c0.c3f453390f97c78700086da77ed330836ec1c59e.jpeg)

### Generative AI-powered learning is on the rise

Generative AI will transform how we learn in 2025, building on ai trends in education that are reshaping the learning landscape. Technology advancements have continually lowered barriers to help more people access quality education. Generative AI-powered learning will open even more opportunities to level the education playing field. Not everyone can have a dedicated, in person tutor, but with generative AI, anyone can have this type of experience embedded in a digital learning system. [Research shows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloom%27s_2_sigma_problem) that one-on-one tutoring vastly improves student performance, and a body of research is starting to show the value of AI tutoring. The generative AI-powered tutor assists you as you learn, understanding your current knowledge and skill level, where you need additional support, and providing recommendations and coaching along your personalized learning path.

### 3

![Image 4: A business meeting in a modern office with a large screen displaying data visualizations, including graphs and a pie chart, as attendees review documents and discuss.](https://d1.awsstatic.com/onedam/marketing-channels/website/aws/en_US/executive-insight/approved/images/beffe1806a05d1cc9644821809b39533.9a1f4edfb6425f5b4d29651e2846a076e03dcec9.jpeg)

### AI trends in education: Digital learning assistants accelerate business outcomes

It’s not just students who will benefit from AI tutors or learning assistants, employees who are upskilling and reskilling will too. For leaders this means your investment in digital training modalities for your employees will generate even greater return on investment. According to a [Harvard study](https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2024/09/professor-tailored-ai-tutor-to-physics-course-engagement-doubled/), adding AI tutoring for “active learning” in its classrooms increased student engagement, motivation, and post-test performance. Your employees can gain that same enhanced learning depth through digital training, allowing you to quickly develop a workforce that has the critical skillsets to contribute to business growth. Simply put, the faster and better your workforce is able to [learn new concepts and skills](https://aws.amazon.com/training/learn-about/generative-ai/) through the power of generative AI, the faster they will be able to help your business innovate and improve the bottom line. I encourage you to check out [AWS SimuLearn](https://skillbuilder.aws/simulearn) in AWS Skill Builder.

### 4

![Image 5: A group of people collaborating in an office, with computer screens displaying code and data.](https://d1.awsstatic.com/onedam/marketing-channels/website/aws/en_US/executive-insight/approved/images/b76b827970510970210c0bc89bd9d980.fdcc41da332e1ba72a58e262a33ba61fe3cb37a7.jpeg)

### Cohort-style training drives long-term business impact

One of the best ways to keep up with the pace of technology is to invest in organization-wide upskilling initiatives that build an engaged culture of learning. However, it can be tough to know how and where to invest in order to maximize your organization’s immediate innovation need. With the interest in generative AI, in particular, we’re seeing more organizations deploy short-term, highly-focused training initiatives on a specific topic, area, or team. The key is to organize a collaborative, cohort-style training that includes dedicated ideation, hands-on learning, and AI soft skills education. These sessions have a couple of key benefits. First, employees come away with actionable use cases that maximize the newly developed skills, giving them priority focus areas that might not have been possible without the collaborative, hands-on learning. Second, with priority initiatives identified, leaders can make quick decisions about redeploying newly-skilled talent into new roles, or investing in additional reskilling. Third, the short-term and focused nature of the training gives the organization quicker results, which reinforce the business benefit of skills development. This leads to greater leadership buy-in for workforce skills initiatives. Given the success we’ve seen in short-term generative AI trainings, I expect more leaders will adopt this approach as they continue to upskill their workforce in 2025 and beyond. Given how quickly generative AI is evolving, speed matters more than ever in the world of technology and business.

### 5

![Image 6: Two people wearing headsets sitting at a desk with computers in a gaming setup, illuminated by blue and red lighting.](https://d1.awsstatic.com/onedam/marketing-channels/website/aws/en_US/executive-insight/approved/images/9c8c7859abb1ae8ca48d86c75fa3223c.7a4ad0d7b32e320b8e9bab8de1744d628680f1dc.jpeg)

### Measuring productivity gains from training efforts

With the rapid pace of technology innovation, training your workforce is no longer a nice-to-do, but a must-do. Ensuring your workforce has the skills to maximize this productivity gain is essential. However, measuring the increased productivity from training, in particular generative AI skills remains elusive. Customers often tell us they don’t know how to measure skill competency or tell if their training is working. This is not a new challenge. But as more leaders recognize the strategic investment in ongoing skills training, it’s resurfacing the need for measurable business value to assign to training initiatives. The short answer is: it’s not always about productivity. It’s a long-game. You are ensuring your team has the right skills to complete the project or initiative so you don’t have to recruit new talent, outsource the work, or worse, shelf the project altogether. Generative AI skills will absolutely make employees more productive, giving you the ability to add new responsibilities to their scope when other, more automated tasks fall away. Measuring the business impact of ongoing training comes down to what can be accomplished that was not possible without the skills development. This takes into account your teams’ engagement, retention, efficiency, collaboration, and confidence to take risks.

Evolution of gen AI
-------------------

None of us can know exactly what the future will bring, given how quickly AI, and its impact on your business and people, is evolving. What you can control is the environment you create that allows your workforce to take on new challenges and opportunities with confidence. Investing in your employees empowers them to build skills that will be paramount to your success, no matter where your roadmap is leading you.

title: Generative artificial intelligence - Wikipedia
content:
In January 2025, the United States Copyright Office (USCO) released extensive guidance regarding the use of AI tools in the creative process, and established that "...generative AI systems also offer tools that similarly allow users to exert control. [These] can enable the user to control the selection and placement of individual creative elements. Whether such modifications rise to the minimum standard of originality required under Feist will depend on a case-by-case determination. In those [...] By mid 2025, despite continued consumer growth, many companies were increasingly abandoning generative AI pilot projects as they had difficulties with integration, data quality and unmet returns, leading analysts to characterize the period as entering the Gartner hype cycle's "trough of disillusionment" phase.(

Applications

[edit] [...] Generative artificial intelligence (Generative AI, GenAI,( or GAI) is a subfield of artificial intelligence that uses generative models to produce text, images, videos, or other forms of data.( These models learn the underlying patterns and structures of their training data and use them to produce new data( based on the input, which often comes in the form of natural language prompts "Prompt (natural language)").(

**Generative artificial intelligence** (**Generative AI**, **GenAI**,**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-1)** or **GAI**) is a subfield of [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") that uses [generative models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_model "Generative model") to produce text, images, videos, or other forms of data.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-4) These models [learn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") the underlying patterns and structures of their [training data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training_data "Training data") and use them to produce new data[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-:02-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-6) based on the input, which often comes in the form of natural language [prompts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prompt_(natural_language) "Prompt (natural language)").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-nytimes2-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-bloomberg2-8)

Generative AI tools have become more common since the [AI boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_boom "AI boom") in the 2020s. This boom was made possible by improvements in [transformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_(machine_learning_model) "Transformer (machine learning model)")-based [deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning")[neural networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_networks "Neural networks"), particularly [large language models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model "Large language model") (LLMs). Major tools include [chatbots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbots "Chatbots") such as [ChatGPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT "ChatGPT"), [Copilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Copilot "Microsoft Copilot"), [Gemini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_(chatbot) "Gemini (chatbot)"), [Claude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_(language_model) "Claude (language model)"), [Grok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grok_(chatbot) "Grok (chatbot)"), and [DeepSeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek_(chatbot) "DeepSeek (chatbot)"); [text-to-image](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-image "Text-to-image") models such as [Stable Diffusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_Diffusion "Stable Diffusion"), [Midjourney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midjourney "Midjourney"), and [DALL-E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DALL-E "DALL-E"); and [text-to-video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-video "Text-to-video") models such as [Veo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veo_(text-to-video_model) "Veo (text-to-video model)") and [Sora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sora_(text-to-video_model) "Sora (text-to-video model)").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-nytimes-gpt4-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-:4-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-auto-13) Technology companies developing generative AI include [OpenAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI "OpenAI"), [xAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XAI_(company) "XAI (company)"), [Anthropic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropic "Anthropic"), [Meta AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_AI "Meta AI"), [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google"), [DeepSeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek "DeepSeek"), and [Baidu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baidu "Baidu").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-nytimes2-7)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-economist1-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-15)

Generative AI is used across many industries, including software development,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-16) healthcare,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-17) finance,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-18) entertainment,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-19) customer service,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-20) sales and marketing,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-economist2-21) art, writing,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-22) fashion,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-mckinsey-23) and product design.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-24) The production of generative AI systems requires large scale data centers using specialized chips which require a lot of electricity for processing and water for cooling.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-25)

Generative AI has raised many ethical questions and governance challenges as it can be used for [cybercrime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cybercrime "Cybercrime"), or to deceive or manipulate people through [fake news](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fake_news "Fake news") or [deepfakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepfake "Deepfake").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-27) Even if used ethically, it may lead to [mass replacement of human jobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technological_unemployment "Technological unemployment").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-28) The tools themselves have been criticized as violating intellectual property laws, since they are trained on copyrighted works.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-29) The material and energy intensity of the AI systems has raised concerns about the [environmental impact of AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_impact_of_AI "Environmental impact of AI"), especially in light of the challenges created by the [energy transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_transition "Energy transition").

History
-------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_artificial_intelligence "History of artificial intelligence")

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early history")]

The first example of an algorithmically generated media is likely the [Markov chain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov_chain "Markov chain"). Markov chains have long been used to model natural languages since their development by Russian mathematician [Andrey Markov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrey_Markov "Andrey Markov") in the early 20th century. Markov published his first paper on the topic in 1906,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-GrinsteadSnell1997page4643-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-Bremaud2013pageIX3-31) and analyzed the pattern of vowels and consonants in the novel _[Eugeny Onegin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugeny\_Onegin "Eugeny Onegin")_ using Markov chains. Once a Markov chain is trained on a [text corpus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_corpus "Text corpus"), it can then be used as a probabilistic text generator.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-33)

Computers were needed to go beyond Markov chains. By the early 1970s, [Harold Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Cohen_(artist) "Harold Cohen (artist)") was creating and exhibiting generative AI works created by [AARON](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AARON "AARON"), the computer program Cohen created to generate paintings.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-34)

The terms generative [AI planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_planning "AI planning") or generative planning were used in the 1980s and 1990s to refer to [AI planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_planning "AI planning") systems, especially [computer-aided process planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-aided_process_planning "Computer-aided process planning"), used to generate sequences of actions to reach a specified goal.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-alting-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-36) Generative AI planning systems used [symbolic AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_AI "Symbolic AI") methods such as [state space search](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_space_search "State space search") and [constraint satisfaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constraint_satisfaction "Constraint satisfaction") and were a "relatively mature" technology by the early 1990s. They were used to generate crisis action plans for military use,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-37) process plans for manufacturing[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-alting-35) and decision plans such as in prototype autonomous spacecraft.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-38)

### Generative neural networks (2014–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Generative neural networks (2014–2019)")]

See also: [Machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") and [deep learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning")

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Discriminative_vs_Generative_Neural_Networks.png/250px-Discriminative_vs_Generative_Neural_Networks.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Discriminative_vs_Generative_Neural_Networks.png)

Above: An [image classifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_classifier "Image classifier"), an example of a neural network trained with a [discriminative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discriminative_model "Discriminative model") objective. Below: A [text-to-image model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-image_model "Text-to-image model"), an example of a network trained with a [generative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_model "Generative model") objective.

Since its inception, the field of [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") has used both [discriminative models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discriminative_model "Discriminative model") and [generative models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_model "Generative model") to model and predict data. Beginning in the late 2000s, the emergence of [deep learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning") drove progress, and research in [image classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_classification "Image classification"), [speech recognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_recognition "Speech recognition"), [natural language processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing "Natural language processing") and other tasks. [Neural networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network "Neural network") in this era were typically trained as [discriminative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discriminative_model "Discriminative model") models due to the difficulty of generative modeling.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-39)

In 2014, advancements such as the [variational autoencoder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variational_autoencoder "Variational autoencoder") and [generative adversarial network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_adversarial_network "Generative adversarial network") produced the first practical deep neural networks capable of learning generative models, as opposed to discriminative ones, for complex data such as images. These deep generative models were the first to output not only class labels for images but also entire images.

In 2017, the [Transformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_(machine_learning_model) "Transformer (machine learning model)") network enabled advancements in generative models compared to older [long short-term memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_short-term_memory "Long short-term memory") (LSTM) models,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-40) leading to the first [generative pre-trained transformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_pre-trained_transformer "Generative pre-trained transformer") (GPT), known as [GPT-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-1 "GPT-1"), in 2018.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-41) This was followed in 2019 by [GPT-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-2 "GPT-2"), which demonstrated the ability to generalize unsupervised to many different tasks as a [Foundation model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foundation_model "Foundation model").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-42)

The new generative models introduced during this period allowed for large neural networks to be trained using [unsupervised learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unsupervised_learning "Unsupervised learning") or [semi-supervised learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-supervised_learning "Semi-supervised learning"), rather than the [supervised learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supervised_learning "Supervised learning") typical of discriminative models. Unsupervised learning removed the need for humans to [manually label data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labeled_data "Labeled data"), allowing for larger networks to be trained.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-43)

### Generative AI boom (2020–)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Generative AI boom (2020–)")]

Main article: [AI boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_boom "AI boom")

[![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Timeline-of-AI-generated-faces.png/250px-Timeline-of-AI-generated-faces.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Timeline-of-AI-generated-faces.png)

AI generated images have become much more advanced.

In March 2020, the release of [15.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15.ai "15.ai"), a free [web application](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_application "Web application") created by an anonymous [MIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIT "MIT") researcher that could generate convincing character voices using minimal training data, marked one of the earliest popular use cases of generative AI.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-44) The platform is credited as the first mainstream service to popularize AI voice cloning ([audio deepfakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_deepfakes "Audio deepfakes")) in [memes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_meme "Internet meme") and [content creation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_creation "Content creation"), influencing subsequent developments in [voice AI technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning_speech_synthesis "Deep learning speech synthesis").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-46)

In 2021, the emergence of [DALL-E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DALL-E "DALL-E"), a [transformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_(machine_learning_model) "Transformer (machine learning model)")-based pixel generative model, marked an advance in AI-generated imagery.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-47) This was followed by the releases of [Midjourney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midjourney "Midjourney") and [Stable Diffusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_Diffusion "Stable Diffusion") in 2022, which further democratized access to high-quality [artificial intelligence art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_art "Artificial intelligence art") creation from [natural language prompts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prompt_engineering "Prompt engineering").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-48) These systems demonstrated unprecedented capabilities in generating photorealistic images, artwork, and designs based on text descriptions, leading to widespread adoption among artists, designers, and the general public.

In late 2022, the public release of [ChatGPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT "ChatGPT") revolutionized the accessibility and [application of generative AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applications_of_artificial_intelligence "Applications of artificial intelligence") for general-purpose text-based tasks.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-49) The system's ability to [engage in natural conversations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbot "Chatbot"), [generate creative content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_art "AI art"), assist with coding, and perform various analytical tasks captured global attention and sparked widespread discussion about AI's potential impact on [work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_in_industry "AI in industry"), [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_in_education "AI in education"), and [creativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_art "AI art").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-51)

In March 2023, [GPT-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-4 "GPT-4")'s release represented another jump in generative AI capabilities. A team from [Microsoft Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Research "Microsoft Research") controversially argued that it "could reasonably be viewed as an early (yet still incomplete) version of an [artificial general intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence "Artificial general intelligence") (AGI) system."[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-Bubeck-2023-52) However, this assessment was contested by other scholars who maintained that generative AI remained "still far from reaching the benchmark of 'general human intelligence'" as of 2023.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-Schlagwein-2023-53) Later in 2023, [Meta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms") released [ImageBind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ImageBind "ImageBind"), an AI model combining multiple [modalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modality_(human%E2%80%93computer_interaction) "Modality (human–computer interaction)") including text, images, video, thermal data, 3D data, audio, and motion, paving the way for more immersive generative AI applications.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-54)

In December 2023, [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google") unveiled [Gemini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_(language_model) "Gemini (language model)"), a multimodal AI model available in four versions: Ultra, Pro, Flash, and Nano.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-AnnounceWSJ-55) The company integrated Gemini Pro into its [Bard chatbot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bard_chatbot "Bard chatbot") and announced plans for "Bard Advanced" powered by the larger Gemini Ultra model.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-56) In February 2024, Google unified Bard and Duet AI under the Gemini brand, launching a mobile app on [Android](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system) "Android (operating system)") and integrating the service into the Google app on [iOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS "IOS").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-57)

In March 2024, [Anthropic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropic "Anthropic") released the [Claude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_(AI) "Claude (AI)") 3 family of large language models, including Claude 3 Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-58) The models demonstrated significant improvements in capabilities across various benchmarks, with Claude 3 Opus notably outperforming leading models from OpenAI and Google.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-59) In June 2024, Anthropic released Claude 3.5 Sonnet, which demonstrated improved performance compared to the larger Claude 3 Opus, particularly in areas such as coding, multistep workflows, and image analysis.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-60)

[![Image 8](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Private_investment_in_generative_AI_-_2024_AI_index.jpg/250px-Private_investment_in_generative_AI_-_2024_AI_index.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Private_investment_in_generative_AI_-_2024_AI_index.jpg)

Private investment in AI (pink) and generative AI (green).

[Asia–Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia%E2%80%93Pacific "Asia–Pacific") countries are significantly more optimistic than Western societies about generative AI and show higher adoption rates. Despite expressing concerns about privacy and the pace of change, in a 2024 survey, 68% of Asia-Pacific respondents believed that AI was having a positive impact on the world, compared to 57% globally.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-61) According to a survey by [SAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAS_Institute "SAS Institute") and Coleman Parkes Research, [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") in particular has emerged as a global leader in generative AI adoption, with 83% of Chinese respondents using the technology, exceeding both the global average of 54% and the U.S. rate of 65%. This leadership is further evidenced by China's [intellectual property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_property_in_China "Intellectual property in China") developments in the field, with a [UN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN "UN") report revealing that Chinese entities filed over 38,000 generative AI [patents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patent "Patent") from 2014 to 2023, substantially surpassing the United States in patent applications.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-62) A 2024 survey on the Chinese social app Soul reported that 18% of respondents born after 2000 used generative AI "almost every day", and that over 60% of respondents like or love AI-generated content, while less than 3% dislike or hate it.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-63)

By mid 2025, despite continued consumer growth, many companies were increasingly abandoning generative AI pilot projects as they had difficulties with integration, data quality and unmet returns, leading analysts to characterize the period as entering the [Gartner hype cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gartner_hype_cycle "Gartner hype cycle")'s "trough of disillusionment" phase.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-65)

Applications
------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Applications")]

Notable types of generative AI models include [generative pre-trained transformers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_pre-trained_transformer "Generative pre-trained transformer") (GPTs), [generative adversarial networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_adversarial_network "Generative adversarial network") (GANs), and [variational autoencoders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variational_autoencoder "Variational autoencoder") (VAEs). Generative AI systems are [_multimodal_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multimodal_learning "Multimodal learning") if they can process multiple types of inputs or generate multiple types of outputs.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-66) For example, [GPT-4o](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-4o "GPT-4o") can both process and generate text, images and audio.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-67)

Generative AI has made its appearance in a wide variety of industries, radically changing the dynamics of content creation, analysis, and delivery. In healthcare,[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-68) for instance, generative AI accelerates [drug discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_discovery "Drug discovery") by creating molecular structures with target characteristics[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-69) and generates [radiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiology "Radiology") images for training diagnostic models. This ability not only enables faster and cheaper development but also enhances medical decision-making. In finance, generative AI services help create datasets and automate reports using natural language. It automates content creation, produces synthetic financial data, and tailors customer communications. It also powers chatbots and virtual agents. Collectively, these technologies enhance efficiency, reduce [operational costs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operational_costs "Operational costs"), and support data-driven decision-making in financial institutions.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-70) The media industry makes use of generative AI for numerous creative activities such as music composition, scriptwriting, video editing, and digital art. The educational sector is impacted as well, since the tools make learning personalized through creating quizzes, study aids, and essay composition. Both the teachers and the learners benefit from AI-based platforms that suit various learning patterns.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-71) In the educational field, in [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia"), student use of [Meta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms")'s generative AI programs resulted in a decline in scores.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-72)

### Audio

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Generative_artificial_intelligence&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Audio")]

See also: [Generative audio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_audio "Generative audio") and [Music and artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_and_artificial_intelligence "Music and artificial intelligence")

Generative AI can also be trained extensively on audio clips to produce natural-sounding [speech synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_synthesis "Speech synthesis") and [text-to-speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-speech "Text-to-speech") capabilities. An early pioneer in this field was [15.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15.ai "15.ai"), launched in March 2020, which demonstrated the ability to clone character voices using as little as 15 seconds of training data.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-80) The website gained widespread attention for its ability to generate emotionally expressive speech for various fictional characters, though it was later taken offline in 2022 due to copyright concerns.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-83) Commercial alternatives subsequently emerged, including [ElevenLabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ElevenLabs "ElevenLabs")' context-aware synthesis tools and [Meta Platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms")'s Voicebox.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-84)

Music generated in 2022 by the Riffusion Inference Server, prompted with `bossa nova with electric guitar`

Generative AI systems such as [MusicLM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MusicLM "MusicLM")[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-85) and MusicGen[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-86) can also be trained on the audio waveforms of recorded music along with text annotations, in order to generate new musical samples based on text descriptions such as _a calming violin melody backed by a distorted guitar riff_.

[Audio deepfakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_deepfake "Audio deepfake") of music [lyrics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyrics "Lyrics") have been generated, like the song Savages, which used AI to mimic rapper [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z")'s vocals. Music artist's instrumentals and lyrics are copyrighted but their voices are not protected from regenerative AI yet, raising a debate about whether artists should get royalties from audio deepfakes.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-87)

Generative AI models are used to power [chatbot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbot "Chatbot") products such as [ChatGPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT "ChatGPT"), [programming tools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_tools "Programming tools") such as [GitHub Copilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GitHub_Copilot "GitHub Copilot"),[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-96)[text-to-image](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text-to-image "Text-to-image") products such as Midjourney, and text-to-video products such as [Runway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runway_(company) "Runway (company)") Gen-2.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-97) Generative AI features have been integrated into a variety of existing commercially available products such as [Microsoft Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Office "Microsoft Office") ([Microsoft Copilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Copilot "Microsoft Copilot")),[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-98)[Google Photos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Photos "Google Photos"),[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence#cite_note-99) and the [Adobe Suite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe_Inc.
